chapter: Los Angeles scene in the 1930s and 40s
title: The Swanee Inn: Ivy Anderson, Margaret Bonds and Calvin Jackson
summary: She recalls the Swanee Inn on Vernon where Nat Cole's trio began and where she worked with Ivy Anderson and double-piano Margaret Bonds and Calvin Jackson.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: remember seeing you at the Club Royal, and one time I even worked the Swanee Inn, and that was -- oh, that was long before I made records. And I worked there one time with wonderful Ivy Anderson. That's a person whose name -- I think we mentioned her earlier, when we were talking about the Chicken Shack.

But I remember Ivy, and I just adored her. She was a wonderful, wonderful woman, and a marvelous artist. I knew her and we worked the Swanee Inn -- that's the place where Nat worked, Nat King Cole first organized the King Cole Trio.
And that place still exists on Vernon Avenue.
I don't think it has music anymore, though. It's just a restaurant.

I don't think so. But that's the place -- at that time -- it shows you how everything has changed -- at that time, they had not one entertainer, but they had continuous entertainment. Because I remember the time I worked there. I worked, accompanying myself, and then Ivy worked there, and then one time Margaret Bonds and Calvin Jackson -- that's somebody -- Calvin Jackson and Margaret Bonds came out here when I first met them. Margaret who, bless her heart, is gone on today, but she was a very marvelous musician,
very marvelous. Did you know her?

Well, she was a marvelous pianist. She was sort of -- really, she wasn't what you'd call a jazz pianist, you know. She was more or less a classical. Because I understand Margaret had a tremendous classical background. I think her mother was a teacher, music teacher, in Chicago. And from people that knew her, and I also got to know her husband later, and her husband was telling me, and other people have told me, that she had a marvelous-- but anyway, she and Calvin Jackson were featured at the Swanee Inn.
Yeah, dual, uh-huh. Double piano. And it was just out of sight, really. But this was the type of thing that used to happen in Los Angeles.

So this is -- I haven't been in the Swanee, and the last time I was there, oh, I guess it's been about -- maybe about four years or better, maybe four or five years ago. Someone was working there then. I can't remember who. I think -- I think Duke Burrell -- do you know Duke Burrell, the piano player?
Duke Burrell was working there at that particular time, but I --
